comment: The one definition of what looks like a secret in text read off the screen, for every platform's helper (ADR-DESK-046).

Each redactor looks at the whole text as read, never at what another left of it, so their order does not matter (owner, 2026-10-08): everything any match takes goes, and one {placeholder} stands for each run of matches that overlap or meet. A match takes itself without what `replacement` copies around {placeholder} at the match's ends; {placeholder} is `placeholder` and $1, $2 are the pattern's groups.
Patterns use the pinned Rust fancy-regex engine on every platform. Native adapters never interpret them. Keep patterns linear on hostile text; the Rust conformance and timing tests are authoritative.
ignoreCase is the only definition flag. Rust compiles this canonical file directly; every platform must pass redaction-cases.json through the linked Rust library.

Every pattern must take time in proportion to the text, whatever the text: no repeat that is scanned again from every position (bound it, or begin the pattern where a run begins). The tests time each on hostile text.

The generator and native regex engines have been retired. Changes must pass the Rust long-continuation, actual-engine-failure and hostile-text timing gates; do not rely on engine-specific pattern rewrites without evidence.

No redactor can hide a secret from another: each finds its secret in the text as read. private-key-cut takes the words of base64 after a header that is cut off, which may hold a later secret's name (the `password` of `password = ...`); that secret's own redactor still finds its value. private-key-body starts only at the start of the text, so that a text starting part-way through a key's line loses that part too. One redactor's matches never overlap each other: each search resumes where the last match's taken part ends (a kept line break may start the next key's lines), and a match must not run over the start of the next secret of its own kind: tokens stop where another of their kind begins, and named-value-up-to-a-name finds a value whose name another value ran into.

A key with a distinctive prefix (AKIA, AIza, ghp_, github_pat_, glpat-, xoxb-, npm_, hf_, whsec_, eyJ, sk_live_) goes wherever it is, even glued to the letters before or after it, as the screen shows a key run into a word or a piece of styling. A pattern whose prefix ordinary words also hold keeps the edge before it, each forced by a near miss in redaction-cases.json: sk- (risk-...), Bearer (pallbearer), the _test_ payment keys (benchmark_test_..., task_test_...). Such a key glued to the word before it, in one piece or in a styled piece the screen shows glued (a link or bold run), stays: owner, 2026-10-08.

redactors.name: private-key-block
redactors.description: A whole private-key block, from its header to its end line.

redactors.name: private-key-cut
redactors.description: A private-key block cut off where the window ends: its header and the words of base64 after it, up to the first character that is not base64 or space (a name or prefix after it may go too; that secret's own redactor still finds its value, as every redactor looks at the text as read).

redactors.name: private-key-end
redactors.description: A private key's body whose header is not in the text, wherever it is (a page read from the middle of a printed key, after a page number or a running header; a header in a font the reader could not draw, a label beside its first full line): the lines of base64 just before its end line, and the end line.

redactors.name: private-key-body
redactors.description: A text that starts inside a private key's body, its header cut off before the text (a page read from the middle of a printed key, a window scrolled past the header): two or more full lines of base64 at the very start, its last, shorter line when that line is one word of base64 (ending its line or running into punctuation), up to the end line if there is one.

redactors.name: private-key-lines
redactors.description: A private key's body wherever it is, whatever is around it (a page of a printed key between a running header and a footer, several pages of one read together, a label beside its first line; lines ended by \n, \r, U+2028 or U+2029): two or more full lines of base64 one after another, a shorter line between them, and the line after them when it is one word of base64 that ends its line or runs into punctuation (owner, 2026-10-08: a key's last line goes even with no digit or symbol, so a lone word such as Done right after them goes too, while a line that goes on with more words stays). A shorter line between full lines goes only when it looks like base64 (a digit, + or /, padding, or a small letter before a capital). Its end line goes with private-key-end. Other runs of such lines (a list of hashes, a base64 blob) go too (owner, 2026-10-05: "redact key bodies anywhere"); one such line alone stays.

redactors.name: json-web-token
redactors.description: A JSON web token: three base64url parts, the first two JSON objects. Its last two parts with the dot before them go alone too, as that is what is left of a token glued to the one before it.

redactors.name: bearer-token
redactors.description: "Bearer <token>", as an Authorization header has it. The word stays. Tokens glued after it, each with its own "Bearer", go with it.

redactors.name: address-password
redactors.description: The password in an address (scheme://user:password@host). The rest stays.

redactors.name: named-value
redactors.description: A value given to a name that says it is secret (password=, api_key:, "token": "…"). The name stays. Only a value with a digit and at least 6 characters, so that "Password: required" stays.

redactors.name: named-value-up-to-a-name
redactors.description: A secret value as named-value has it, ending where another secret name given a value begins inside it (token=<value>,password: <value>), so that the second value is found too; named-value still takes the whole run, as a value may hold such a name.

redactors.name: api-key-sk
redactors.description: Keys starting "sk-" (several AI providers).

redactors.name: payment-key
redactors.description: Payment provider keys (secret, restricted, publishable; live or test); a key glued to another stops where the next begins, and test keys glued after it go with it.

redactors.name: webhook-secret
redactors.description: Webhook signing secrets, each ending where another of its kind glued to it begins.

redactors.name: github-token
redactors.description: GitHub tokens, each ending where another of its kind glued to it begins.

redactors.name: github-fine-grained-token
redactors.description: GitHub fine-grained tokens.

redactors.name: gitlab-token
redactors.description: GitLab tokens.

redactors.name: aws-access-key-id
redactors.description: AWS access key ids.

redactors.name: google-api-key
redactors.description: Google API keys.

redactors.name: slack-token
redactors.description: Slack tokens.

redactors.name: npm-token
redactors.description: npm tokens, each ending where another of its kind glued to it begins.

redactors.name: hugging-face-token
redactors.description: Hugging Face tokens, each ending where another of its kind glued to it begins.
